## Procedure and coverage

No step-by-step procedure was supplied.

- README version table: "Tested by running the camera code in a PC emulator, independently reviewed, then field-tested on the owner's camera."
- DEVELOPMENT.md describes the pre-camera checks in general (a byte oracle against the last passing image, reference and runtime-zone censuses, MN10300 emulation on the camera's own key, paint and dial routes with negative controls, mutant images and two independent audits; about 43 stages for a release).
- The colour wheel guide says its sections 1 to 7 (controls, values, mode guide, moved art filters, limits) are confirmed on a camera; its example recipes are not tested.
- The colour wheel was worked on in internal builds 57 to 86 on the owner's camera; those builds are not released.

## Limits and assumptions

- One owner and one camera; never tried on another body and not reproduced by the Atlas.
- The builder's expected result is published only as SHA-1 2d34ed2deba4f3d3a838b263ef201ac114dc4c22; no SHA-256 of the installed file was reported. The release's SHA-256s are for the builder exe and zip, not the firmware.
- No test date or per-step results; not stated whether the version 56 test list was re-run on 87.
- The emulator and harness are unpublished and no stage results, logs or audit reports for 87 are given, so the emulation is recorded here as part of the maintainer's account, not as separate emulator evidence.
- DEVELOPMENT.md says the re-entrancy defect class, the class of the 87 Contrast/Gradation fix, is covered by design review and stress emulation and is not proven by the harness.
- Known in 87: the ART mode guide still shows the P icon; very dark and very pale pixels in an edited sector can spread a little into neighbouring colours.
- reported_on is the release date of v87, not the date of the field test.
